Our work in statistical genetics develops probabilistic and computational models to uncover demographic history, recombination patterns, natural selection, and complex trait architecture from high-dimensional genomic data. A central contribution is [**MOSAIC**](../software.qmd), a two-layer Hidden Markov Model for multiway local ancestry inference that reconstructs historical admixture events without requiring direct surrogate reference populations.

Recent and ongoing collaborations span human biobank cohorts (quantifying group-structure effects on polygenic risk scores in the UK Biobank and mitonuclear discordance in Parkinson's disease), livestock and equine functional genomics (mitonuclear coadaptation and trypanotolerance in hybrid African cattle; imputation and exercise genomics in Thoroughbred horses), and bacterial comparative genomics.
